input: Build a emergency go-bag for natural disasters

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The number and type of people (adults, children, elderly, pets) directly determines quantities, item types, and medical considerations included in the bag.
The specific natural disasters most relevant to the user's location (earthquake, hurricane, wildfire, flood, etc.) change which supplies are prioritized — e.g., dust masks vs. life jackets.
A budget ceiling determines whether the user buys a pre-made kit, sources items individually, or repurposes things they already own.
Whether the bag is for home, a car, or both — and the climate/terrain of the user's area — affects bag size, weight limits, and climate-specific items like hand warmers or cooling towels.
Knowing how long the bag needs to sustain the user (72 hours is standard, but some scenarios require a week+) determines the volume of food, water, and supplies needed.
Some people want a lightweight, minimal bag they can grab fast; others want a comprehensive, heavy-duty kit. This shapes every item trade-off.
Understanding whether the user is starting from scratch or topping up an existing bag determines how much foundational guidance vs. gap-filling advice to provide.

gold.taskTitle: Build a Natural Disaster Emergency Go-Bag
gold.taskDescription: Assemble a ready-to-grab emergency bag stocked with supplies to sustain the user during a natural disaster evacuation or displacement.

questions.title: How many people and pets is this bag covering?
questions.description: Identify the exact number of adults, children, elderly individuals, and pets the go-bag must support to calibrate quantities and special needs items.

questions.title: Which natural disasters are most likely in your area?
questions.description: Pinpoint the 1-3 disaster types most relevant to the user's region (e.g., wildfire, earthquake, hurricane) so the bag contents can be prioritized accordingly.

questions.title: What is your total budget for this go-bag?
questions.description: Establish a spending limit to determine whether to buy a pre-built kit, shop individually, or repurpose existing household items.

questions.title: Where will the bag be stored and used — home or car?
questions.description: Determine the primary location and environment for the bag, which affects size, weight, and climate-specific item choices.

questions.title: How many days of self-sufficiency should the bag cover?
questions.description: Decide on the target duration (e.g., 72 hours, 1 week) to correctly size food, water, medication, and consumable supplies.

questions.title: Do you prefer a lightweight grab-and-go or a comprehensive heavy kit?
questions.description: Clarify the user's priority between portability and completeness, which drives every item trade-off in the packing list.

questions.title: Are you building from scratch or upgrading an existing bag?
questions.description: Determine the user's starting point to decide whether to provide a full foundational checklist or focus on identifying and filling specific gaps.
